title: Controlled NCCL bandwidth reproduction, 3-node DGX Spark

harness.distribution_method: Dockerfile shipped to each node; image built locally on all three (no 9.6 GB image transfer). Runtime NCCL version verified independently on sparkmain, spark1, spark2.

notes.mpi_oob: mpirun's own OOB/BTL always used the management LAN (wlP9s9). The fabric is a set of point-to-point /30 links, NOT a full mesh, so MPI's TCP BTL cannot route across it. MPI is only a process launcher here; the variable under test is NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME, which selects NCCL's own bootstrap channel.
notes.transport_validation: Every run's NCCL_DEBUG confirmed via NET/IB/*. Zero occurrences of NET/Socket in any run. No run was void.
notes.correctness: Every run reported #wrong = 0 out-of-place and in-place.
notes.columns: algbw/busbw reported for BOTH out-of-place (oop, the published convention) and in-place (ip).

runs.note: COLD-START OUTLIER on the out-of-place column (4651.96 us vs ~1300 us in repeats). Superseded by rep2/rep3.
No merged virtual devices created; all four physical HCAs used individually.
Auto discovery finds exactly the same four HCAs and builds the same two merged pairs as the explicit list.

conclusions.headline: The gap does not exist. With the official version-matched harness, the CURRENT config (variant A, unchanged) already delivers 23.92 GB/s busbw at 16 GiB and ~16-17 GB/s at 32 MiB on 3 ranks. The published comparison points are 20.84 @16GiB and 18.70 @32MiB. We match or exceed them.
conclusions.which_variable_moved_the_number: NONE of A/B/C/D moved it. Bootstrap interface (A vs B), NIC merging (B vs C), and HCA discovery (B vs D) are all within noise at 16 GiB: 23.92 / 23.94 / 23.86 / 23.85 GB/s, a spread of 0.4%. The ONLY variable that mattered was the HARNESS itself.
conclusions.old_5_80_figure: The prior 5.80 GB/s came from the custom PyTorch harness at 64 MiB, not from the fabric. Replacing it with official all_gather_perf raises the same 3-rank ring config to 23.92 GB/s. The custom harness was measuring itself.
conclusions.merge_question_answered: NCCL does merge ACROSS physical ports: 'Made virtual device [4] name=rocep1s0f0+rocep1s0f1' and '[5] name=roceP2p1s0f0+roceP2p1s0f1'. The BANDWIDTH-COMPARISON hypothesis that this cross-port pairing would harm a 3-node ring is REFUTED by variant C: turning merging off entirely (four separate NET/IB/0-3 devices) produced 23.86 vs 23.86 GB/s at 16 GiB. Cross-port merging is harmless here.
conclusions.ceiling: 23.85-23.94 GB/s at 16 GiB across every 3-rank variant, essentially pinned to the ~24 GB/s PCIe Gen5 x4 ceiling documented in BANDWIDTH-COMPARISON.md. The fabric is saturating PCIe, not underperforming.
conclusions.world2_vs_world3: 3-rank (23.92) slightly EXCEEDS 2-rank (22.30) busbw at 16 GiB out-of-place. There is no rank-count penalty; the earlier claim that the deficit grew with rank count was an artifact of the custom harness.
conclusions.size_dependence: Real and matches published curves: ~16-17 GB/s at 32 MiB rising to ~24 GB/s at 16 GiB, about +45%.

docs_needing_correction: docs/BANDWIDTH-COMPARISON.md: the '~3.2x gap' headline is refuted. The gap was harness, not fabric.
docs/BANDWIDTH-COMPARISON.md: the cross-port merge hypothesis (f0+f1 spanning two neighbours) is measured and refuted by variant C.
docs/BANDWIDTH-NEXT-TEST.md: 'bootstrap is the strongest lead' is refuted; bootstrap interface made no measurable difference.
The ~24 GB/s PCIe ceiling estimate in BANDWIDTH-COMPARISON.md is CONFIRMED and is where we actually sit.
